title: Slow Cooker Ham, Cabbage & Potato Soup
description: A low-effort slow-cooker soup that turns ham, cabbage, potatoes, and ordinary pantry seasonings into a cozy dinner.

ingredients.item: russet or yellow potatoes, cut in 1-inch pieces

substitutions: Use smoked turkey instead of ham.
Use frozen diced potatoes if that makes prep easier.
Add 1 drained can white beans for a heartier soup.

steps.text: Put everything in the slow cooker.
Cook until the potatoes and cabbage are tender.

cookSteps.text: Put 4 cups chopped cabbage, 1 1/2 pounds potatoes, 2 cups diced cooked ham, 1 chopped onion, 5 cups chicken broth, and the garlic powder and pepper if using into the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on LOW for about 6 hours, or until the potatoes are tender and the cabbage is soft.
Stir well. Taste before adding salt because ham and broth can already be salty. Ladle into bowls and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 2 months. Reheat until steaming hot.

title: Sheet-Pan Sausage, Cabbage & Pears
description: Smoky sausage, sweet pear, and tender browned cabbage roast together on one pan for a simple cool-weather dinner.

ingredients.item: firm pears, cored and cut in wedges

substitutions: Use turkey or chicken smoked sausage.
Use firm apples instead of pears.
Leave out mustard if you prefer a milder flavor.

steps.text: Season the sausage, cabbage, and pears.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Put 12 ounces sliced smoked sausage, 5 cups chopped cabbage, and 2 wedged firm pears on a large sheet pan.
Drizzle with 1 1/2 tablespoons oil. Add 1 tablespoon mustard and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder if using, then toss well and spread into an even layer.
Roast 20 minutes. Stir, then roast another 5 minutes or until the cabbage edges are browned and the pears are tender.
Serve hot. Add salt and pepper only after tasting the sausage.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat on a sheet pan or in a skillet until steaming hot.

title: Leftover Taco Meat & Cheesy Rice Skillet
description: Leftover taco meat and cooked rice become a hot cheesy skillet meal in about 15 minutes.
substitutions: Use cooked ground turkey, beef, chicken, or beans seasoned for tacos.
Use canned diced tomatoes instead of salsa and season to taste.
Use Monterey Jack instead of cheddar.

steps.text: Heat the rice, taco meat, and salsa.

cookSteps.text: Put 2 cups cooked rice, 1 1/2 cups cooked taco meat, 3/4 cup salsa, 1/2 cup water, and 1 cup frozen corn if using in a large skillet.
Cook over medium heat for 6–7 minutes, stirring often, until everything is steaming hot. Add another splash of water if the rice looks dry.
Sprinkle 1 cup shredded cheddar over the top. Cover for 2–3 minutes, until the cheese melts.

storage: Use the taco meat and rice only while they are within their original safe refrigerated storage windows. Refrigerate the finished skillet up to 3 days and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Small-Batch Brown Sugar Apple Cookies
description: A single apple makes a small tray of soft brown-sugar cookies with familiar pantry ingredients.
substitutions: Leave out cinnamon for plain brown-sugar apple cookies.
Use a firm pear instead of apple.
Chill very juicy diced fruit on a paper towel for a few minutes before mixing it in.

steps.text: Mix a small batch of apple cookie dough.
Bake until the edges are set.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Line or lightly grease a sheet pan.
Stir 3 tablespoons softened butter and 1/4 cup packed brown sugar until creamy. Mix in 1 egg yolk.
Stir in 1/2 cup flour, 1/4 teaspoon baking soda, and 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon if using. Fold in 1/2 cup finely diced apple.
Drop 8 rounded spoonfuls onto the pan and flatten them slightly. Bake 10–12 minutes, until the edges are set and lightly browned.
Cool on the pan for 5 minutes before moving the cookies.

storage: Store covered at room temperature for 1 day or refrigerate up to 4 days because the fresh apple keeps the cookies moist.
